voice.name: Sulafat
voice.style: 溫和、好奇的說書人語氣，台灣國語，語速適中

look.style: flat cartoon editorial illustration, clean dark outlines, warm muted palette of cream, teal and brick red, soft paper grain, simple rounded shapes, generic friendly faces
look.negative: text, letters, readable numbers, logos, brand names, watermark, photorealistic, extra fingers, deformed hands, blurry

music.prompt: light pizzicato strings and soft marimba, curious and warm, documentary explainer mood, no vocals

youtube.title: 結帳嗶一聲，那串條碼是誰發的號碼？
youtube.description: 每天結帳都會聽到嗶的一聲，但那串黑白線條不是隨便印的，而是一組要付費才拿得到的號碼。這一集從一九四八年費城的一個研究生講起，看幾條線怎麼變成全世界共用的號碼簿。

data.prompt: a friendly cashier at a supermarket checkout sliding a cereal box over a glowing red scanner window, a short queue of shoppers with baskets behind, warm evening light, the stripe pattern on the box catching the red glow
data.camera: slow push in toward the scanner window

lines.text: 結帳時嗶的一聲，收銀機就知道你買了什麼。
那串黑白線條，其實是一組要付費的號碼。

data.prompt: a giant open ledger floating above rows of shop shelves, every page lined with rows of plain black and white stripe patterns, tiny clerks on ladders stamping new pages
data.camera: slow pan left across the pages

lines.text: 品牌每年付費，才拿得到全世界不重複的號碼。
今天就來看，幾條線怎麼變成一門生意。

data.prompt: a 1940s university corridor with tall windows, a young graduate student in a tweed jacket with notebooks under his arm, pausing to overhear two men in suits talking by an office door
data.camera: slow pan right along the corridor

lines.text: 一九四八年，費城有個研究生叫席爾佛。
他聽說有家超市，想讓結帳自動記下商品。

data.prompt: a young man in 1940s summer clothes kneeling on a quiet beach, drawing long parallel lines in the sand with four fingers, a row of dots and dashes above them, gentle waves and a bright afternoon sky
data.camera: tilt down from the sky to the lines in the sand

lines.text: 他的朋友伍德蘭，坐在海灘上想辦法。
他把摩斯電碼的點和線，在沙上往下拉長。

data.prompt: two young inventors at a cluttered wooden desk in 1949, a large technical drawing of stripes and a round ring pattern spread between them, a desk lamp and an envelope ready to mail
data.camera: slow push in on the drawing

lines.text: 兩人在一九四九年申請了專利。
三年後，專利真的下來了。

data.prompt: a dusty workshop shelf holding a bulky early reading machine under a cloth, a wall calendar shedding its pages, afternoon dust floating in a beam of light
data.camera: static frame with a gentle drift

lines.text: 可是那個年代，還沒有又快又便宜的機器讀得動它。
這個點子一放，就是二十多年。

data.prompt: a 1970s supermarket checkout, a cashier holding a small pack of chewing gum over a new glass scanner window, store staff and a photographer gathered around to watch
data.camera: tilt up from the scanner to the faces

lines.text: 一九七四年六月，俄亥俄州一家超市掃了第一件商品。
那是一包口香糖。

data.prompt: a friendly clerk at a huge wooden card catalogue handing out small cards printed with stripe patterns to a queue of a baker, a farmer and a toy maker
data.camera: pull back to show the whole queue

lines.text: 條碼前面那一段，是廠商自己的代碼。
代碼由國際條碼組織發出，廠商每年付費續用。

data.prompt: a modern checkout counter, a hand holding a snack box printed with a small square dot pattern beside a row of stripes, a scanner window glowing, soft daylight
data.camera: slow pan right past the counter

lines.text: 現在，零售業正準備讓收銀機也讀得懂二維碼。
一個小方塊，能裝下多很多的資訊。

data.prompt: a city at dusk seen from above, thin glowing threads running from shops, trucks and warehouses to one enormous open book floating in the sky
data.camera: slow crane up over the city

lines.text: 條碼真正厲害的，不是那幾條線。
而是一本大家都願意付費加入的號碼簿。

data.title: 下一個故事：另一個天天在用的標準

lines.text: 所以嗶的那一聲，其實是在查一本全世界共用的號碼簿。
下一個故事，我們聊另一個天天在用、卻很少人注意的標準。
